title: Satisfiability via component labels
statement: Let $q$ be a nonnegative integer and let $G$ be a finite unique game with a nonempty set of variables and a nonempty set of constraints. Each constraint joins two distinct variables, carries a permutation of the $q$ labels, and every variable occurs in some constraint. The game has a labeling satisfying every constraint if and only if there is a choice of one label for each connected component such that propagating those labels along component paths gives a labeling satisfying every constraint.
hypotheses_covered: The variable set is finite and nonempty
The constraint set is finite and nonempty
Each constraint carries a permutation of the labels
Every variable participates in a constraint
